reason: As written the RANSAC experiment is runnable (python3, GF(2^n) bitmask arithmetic, n<=23, minutes) and has a built-in positive control (alpha=tau gives x^2, exact k=1 agreement) and a natural null (random function: agreement = k+1 fitted points + ~0). But it is a statistical test of a question already decided exactly by degree. x([alpha]P)=R_alpha(x(P)) with R_alpha a rational function of degree N(alpha) (N(1+tau)=2, N(1-tau)=4, N(2)=4, N(tau^2+1)=2; e.g. x([2]P)=x^2+b/x^2 on y^2+xy=x^3+ax^2+b). An additive L of 2-degree k has polynomial degree 2^k. If L agrees with R_alpha on more than 2^k+N(alpha) distinct x, then L*den-num (degree <=2^k+N(alpha)) vanishes identically, so R_alpha is itself additive. So agreement is either <=2^k+N(alpha) points (fraction <=(2^k+N)/2^n -> 0 whenever k<n-c) or R_alpha is exactly additive, which is a finite symbolic check. The stated prediction bound '(k+3)/2^n|E|' is mis-stated: the Bezout bound is 2^k+N(alpha), not k+3, so as written the prediction_if_true can be violated by legitimate agreement of up to 2^k+N points (k=6: 66 points) and the test could report a spurious 'reopening'. RANSAC is also unnecessary: the model is linear in the k+1 coefficients, so agreement-maximisation is exact linear algebra/decoding (Reed-Solomon-like list decoding of a degree-2^k polynomial), no random trials needed. Scaling to n=131: the Bezout bound is n-independent (polynomial degree identity), so the toy transfers rigorously, not just empirically; the toy adds nothing beyond the proof. Success metric (agreement count, rank of coefficient system, additivity residual of R_alpha) is structural, not wall time. Deeper obstruction the toy does not address: any coordinate f with f([alpha]P)=L(f(P)) for the ring Z[tau] would make f a homomorphism E(F_q)->(F_q,+); E(F_q) has odd prime order r (K_0: 4*r), (F_q,+) is a 2-group, so the image has order <=4: Hom(E,G_a)=0 (E complete) is the real Drinfeld-vs-EC difference (the Drinfeld module IS a G_a with twisted F_q[T]-action, E is not affine). Classification: closure with measurement, relabelling-class; no advance; no security claim.
fix: Replace RANSAC by an exact, cheaper, falsifiable design. (1) Symbolic arm (gp, seconds): for K_0 (y^2+xy=x^3+1 over F_2) compute R_alpha(x) in F_2(x) for alpha in {1+tau, 2, 1-tau, tau^2+1, tau^j j=1..6, tau^j+1, 2tau, 3} by iterating the tau and group-law x-maps (x(P+Q) formula with Q=tau P, y eliminated via the curve, or ellmul on the generic point over F_2(x)[y]/(curve)); record deg R_alpha (must equal N(alpha)), and test additivity exactly: R(x+t)-R(x)-R(t) == 0 in F_2(x,t). Metric = additivity residual rank / number of nonzero terms; also report the 'distance to additive' = minimal 2-degree k and number of non-additive monomials. Prediction_if_true: only alpha in tau^j * {+-1} (units times Frobenius powers) have zero residual; all others have a pole (denominator of degree >0) hence not even polynomial. Prediction_if_false: some non-Frobenius alpha has residual 0 (would be a proof, not a statistic). (2) Numeric arm to validate the bound, not to discover: for n in {13,17,19,23}, k in 1..6, take ALL (n<=17) or a 2^16-point sample of x in F_{2^n}, compute y_alpha(x)=R_alpha(x) from the curve, and compute exact max agreement with any additive L of 2-degree k by solving the (k+1)-unknown F_{2^n}-linear system over random (k+1)-subsets plus consensus counting, OR directly by evaluating the Bezout bound; assert agreement <= 2^k+N(alpha). Controls: positive = alpha=tau^j with k>=j (agreement = 100%); negative = random function on the same domain with matched fitting freedom (expect k+1+O(2^-n*2^16)); also a 'planted' control = R = x^2 + (noise on epsilon fraction) to show the fitter recovers a true additive law at fraction 1-epsilon. (3) Add the coordinate-generalisation arm that the idea actually needs for lever 14: replace x by an arbitrary F_q-coordinate h(x) of low degree (h = (ax+b)/(cx+d), or y/x, or x+x^{-1}) and test additivity of h∘R_alpha∘h^{-1}; and test the group-theoretic obstruction numerically: the F_2-linear span of {x(P)} over a point set does not carry a Z[tau]-module structure, i.e. check that no nonzero F_2-linear map E(F_q)->F_q commutes with tau (trivial since |E| odd part r). (4) State the n=131 transfer as the theorem 'agreement <= 2^k+N(alpha) independent of n; k would need to be >= n-O(1) for positive density, at which point L has n free F_q coefficients and is a generic interpolant (no content)'. Cost: gp arm < 1 CPU-min, numeric arm < 5 CPU-min.
